props.title: Skippy and the Intruders

sections.content: **Skippy and the Intruders** (1969) represents a fascinating entry in Australia's early family entertainment, building on the success of the **Skippy the Bush Kangaroo** TV series (1966-1969). Like Storm Boy (1976) and Dot and the Kangaroo (1977), it showcases Australia's unique wildlife while delivering adventure aimed at younger viewers. The film follows Sonny Hammond and his pet kangaroo Skippy as they uncover criminal activity in Waratah National Park, establishing a template that later Australian family films like **BMX Bandits** (1983) would follow.

sections.content: The film captures a pivotal moment in Australian cinema, coming just before the Australian New Wave of the 1970s with films like Wake in Fright (1971) and Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975). While those later films explored darker themes, **Skippy and the Intruders** (1969) maintained the wholesome family entertainment style that characterized much of Australia's early screen output. The film's success helped prove there was an audience for Australian-made family content.

The environmental themes present in **Skippy and the Intruders** (1969) were ahead of their time, predating the eco-conscious wave of films like **Long Weekend** (1978) and **The Last Wave** (1977). The film's portrayal of the Australian bush as both beautiful and potentially dangerous would become a recurring motif in Australian cinema, later seen in everything from **Razorback** (1984) to **Black Water** (2007). sections.content: The production techniques used in **Skippy and the Intruders** (1969) influenced later Australian wildlife features, establishing practical methods for filming with animals that would be utilized in films like **Mad Dog Morgan** (1976) and **The Man from Snowy River** (1982). The film's success also helped establish international interest in Australian locations and wildlife, paving the way for later successes like **Crocodile Dundee** (1986).
